payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism. Following an independent audit, its governing cycle-life figure is 8,400 cycles; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted. The prototype achieved 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
